question: Which of the following correctly describes direct ophthalmoscopy compared to indirect ophthalmoscopy?

answers.text: Direct ophthalmoscopy provides a wider field of view and is preferred for peripheral retinal examination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Indirect ophthalmoscopy provides a wider field of view (up to 60°) and is preferred for peripheral retinal examination.

answers.text: Direct ophthalmoscopy produces an inverted real image with high magnification (~15×) and a narrow field of view (~5°)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Direct ophthalmoscopy produces an upright virtual image (not inverted) — wait, but it gives ~15× magnification and only ~5° field of view, making it ideal for disc and macula detail, not periphery.

answers.text: Direct ophthalmoscopy requires a condensing lens held in front of the patient's eye

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. It is indirect ophthalmoscopy that requires a condensing lens (e.g., 20D or 28D). Direct ophthalmoscopy does not use a condensing lens.

answers.text: Direct ophthalmoscopy produces an inverted image, making it more difficult to interpret than indirect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Direct ophthalmoscopy produces an upright virtual image. It is indirect ophthalmoscopy that produces an inverted real image.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key distinction: direct = upright image, high magnification, narrow field; indirect = inverted image, lower magnification, wide field. Review the optical principles section.
Well done. Direct ophthalmoscopy: upright virtual image, ~15× magnification, ~5° field — excellent for disc and macula detail.
